name: olai-plugin-opencode
//name: UNSCOPED, like every other tenant: `@olai/*` is the scope for the packages that ARE olai, and an ENGINE is somebody else's agent with olai's judgement about it on top — the closest thing in this tree to a plugin written outside it. The directory is the plugin word (`opencode`), which is the row's `id`, the word `--plugins` takes, and the address of its docs page.
//exports: FIVE, and the split is the tree's three-door rule with nothing added. `./server` is what the row mounts: the leg, the probe that looks for `opencode` on the agent search path, and the install sentence — no `solid-js` anywhere on that graph. `./browser` is the chunk the tab fetches when the roster names this plugin, and it carries exactly one face: the mark this engine wears in a transcript's speaker column. The ROOT is the wire identity and nothing more — this plugin composes no sibling surface. `./testids` and `./all.css` are the two contracts the generated bundle files need of every row.
//: THE OPENCODE ENGINE — the leg that reads its wire, the probe that finds it on this host, and the mark it wears. The plainest of the three: plain ACP over stdio, no pin of olai's, no adapter to ship, and a leg that is mostly `null`s — each of which was a request that would otherwise be sent and refused.
//dependencies: `@olai/acp/engine` is the shape both ends spell — the leg, the adapter, the registration — and it is a floor package under both this plugin and `@olai/chat`, which is what lets neither import the other. `@olai/plugin-api` is the door: the `Agents` tag its `./server` registers into, and the slot service its `./browser` hangs a mark in. `effect` because a plugin's `apply` is one. `solid-js` because the mark is a component.
//devDependencies: The protocol SDK for `PermissionOption`, in the leg's OWN bench alone: the leg itself names none of the SDK's types (`@olai/acp/engine` carries the ones a leg's signatures need), and the fixtures that stage a permission request do. Type-only, so no SDK code and no zod enter this package's closure.
